complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Create comprehensive mock API service for frontend development
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down the mock API service implementation into specific technical tasks including MSW setup, Korean data generation with Faker.js, individual API endpoint implementations, network simulation, TypeScript type definitions, and persistence layer. Each subtask should focus on a specific aspect of the mock service that can be developed and tested independently.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task requires implementing a complete mock API infrastructure with multiple endpoints, realistic Korean data generation, network simulation, error scenarios, TypeScript integration, and persistence. The complexity stems from needing to accurately simulate backend behavior, handle Korean language/address formats, implement multiple API endpoints with different behaviors, and ensure seamless integration with frontend components.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Organize the testing infrastructure setup into distinct phases: Vitest configuration, React Testing Library setup with Next.js utilities, MSW integration for test mocking, Playwright E2E setup, creation of test suites for critical components, and CI/CD pipeline configuration. Each subtask should produce a working part of the testing infrastructure that can be verified independently.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Setting up a comprehensive testing infrastructure involves multiple testing frameworks (Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright), integration with existing mock services, custom utilities for Next.js and Naver Maps mocking, and CI/CD automation. The complexity comes from coordinating these different tools and ensuring they work together seamlessly.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Build Search Interface and Filtering Components
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Divide the search interface implementation into focused components: debounced SearchBar, accessible AutocompleteDropdown with keyboard navigation, FilterPanel with card/category management, SearchResults with dual view modes, centralized filter state management, URL parameter synchronization, and comprehensive loading/error states. Each component should be self-contained and testable.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task involves complex UI interactions including debouncing, keyboard navigation, state management, URL synchronization, and multiple view modes. The integration with the mock API service and need for responsive, accessible components with proper error handling adds significant complexity.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Structure the route planning implementation as: mock API integration verification, RoutePlanner component with origin/destination inputs, WaypointList with drag-and-drop functionality, map polyline visualization, DirectionsList for turn-by-turn navigation, and route sharing/persistence features. Focus on creating reusable components that integrate smoothly with the existing map infrastructure.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: While still complex, this task builds upon existing map components and mock API infrastructure. The main challenges are implementing drag-and-drop functionality, polyline rendering on Naver Maps, and managing route state. The complexity is moderate as it leverages work from previous tasks.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Enhance TypeScript Definitions for Naver Maps
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Create TypeScript definitions in phases: core map and marker interfaces, event system with proper generics, advanced features (overlays, controls, utilities), and runtime type guards with documentation. Each phase should be independently usable and thoroughly documented with JSDoc comments.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is primarily a TypeScript definition task that requires understanding the Naver Maps API surface but doesn't involve complex implementation logic. The work is straightforward but detailed, requiring careful API documentation review and type modeling.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Plan the state management migration systematically: analyze current implementation and design new architecture, implement core Zustand stores with TypeScript, add performance optimizations and computed values, integrate debugging tools, implement persistence and hydration, and migrate all components from Context API. Each step should maintain application functionality while improving performance.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Migrating from Context API to Zustand while fixing circular dependencies requires careful analysis and planning. The complexity comes from needing to maintain functionality during migration, implementing performance optimizations, ensuring SSR compatibility, and coordinating state across multiple stores without reintroducing circular dependencies.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Implement SEO and performance optimizations incrementally: Next.js 14 metadata API for dynamic meta tags, structured data with JSON-LD for local businesses, XML sitemap generation, comprehensive image optimization with next/image, intelligent prefetching and resource hints, and Core Web Vitals optimization. Each optimization should be measurable and independently verifiable.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task requires deep knowledge of Next.js 14 features, SEO best practices, and performance optimization techniques. The complexity stems from needing to coordinate multiple optimization strategies, implement Korean-specific SEO considerations, and achieve specific Core Web Vitals targets while maintaining functionality.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Build PWA features progressively: Workbox service worker setup, offline-first caching strategies for API and assets, map tile caching system, web app manifest with icons, push notification infrastructure, custom install prompts with A2HS flow, and Lighthouse PWA optimization. Each feature should enhance the offline experience while maintaining performance.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Implementing a full PWA requires coordinating multiple complex features including service workers, caching strategies, push notifications, and offline functionality. The complexity is high due to map tile caching, Korean localization needs, cross-browser compatibility requirements, and achieving Lighthouse PWA scores > 95.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Setup Spring Boot Backend Project with Database and API Structure
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Establish the backend infrastructure systematically: Spring Boot project initialization with Java 21, multi-module architecture setup, PostgreSQL with PostGIS configuration, JPA entities with spatial support, spatial indexes and optimizations, repository layer with location queries, service layer with caching, REST controllers with validation, security and CORS configuration, and monitoring/logging setup. Each component should be independently testable and follow Spring best practices.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is the most complex task as it involves setting up an entire backend infrastructure from scratch. It requires expertise in Spring Boot, PostgreSQL with PostGIS for spatial queries, JPA with spatial types, caching, security, and monitoring. The complexity comes from integrating multiple technologies and ensuring proper architecture for scalability.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement public API integration and data collection system for Korean welfare cards
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Build the data collection system in phases: research and document Korean public APIs, design modular API client architecture, implement WebClient-based HTTP clients, add resilience patterns (retry/circuit breaker), create data transformation layer with Korean address handling, implement Spring Batch jobs for synchronization, build incremental update mechanism, create data quality validation, implement monitoring and alerting, and comprehensive documentation. Each phase should be production-ready and maintainable.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task has the highest complexity due to integration with multiple Korean government APIs, handling various data formats, implementing batch processing at scale, Korean-specific data validation (addresses, business numbers), and building a resilient system with monitoring. It requires expertise in Spring Batch, external API integration, data quality assurance, and Korean data standards.
